title: FBI Seizes $1.2 Billion in Crypto Stolen from Binance in Historic Heist
meta_title: FBI Seizes $1.2 Billion in Crypto Stolen from Binance
meta_description: The FBI has seized over $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance in history's largest crypto heist, linking the attack to North Korea.
discover_titles: FBI Seizes $1.2 Billion in Crypto Stolen From Binance
U.S. Recovers $1.2 Billion From Historic Binance Crypto Heist
FBI Blames North Korea for Massive Binance Crypto Theft
spot: The FBI announced Thursday it has seized more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance last month during the largest crypto heist in history, attributing the cybercrime to North Korean hackers.
content_html:
Key Developments

The Federal Bureau of Investigation announced on Thursday that law enforcement has successfully seized over $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency that was reported stolen last month from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. The incident stems from a staggering theft of approximately $6.3 billion, widely regarded as the biggest crypto heist in recorded history. The FBI has previously attributed the massive security breach to a North Korean hacking collective known as TraderTraitor.

Overall, the U.S. government and private sector partners have combined forces to freeze more than $2.7 billion of the total stolen funds. The U.S. Department of Justice stated that it has officially obtained court authorization to seize or restrain over $1.2 billion of that amount. Typically, the government initiates this process by filing a claim of forfeiture with a judge, who then decides the rightful ownership for returning recovered funds to legitimate claimants.

In addition to the Binance recovery, the FBI also highlighted a separate North Korean cyber operation. Officials disclosed that a social engineering scheme dubbed FaceStealer has resulted in the theft of $400 million in cryptocurrency over the past 18 months, utilizing hijacked messaging apps and deepfake videos.

Key Takeaways

  • Historic Recovery: The FBI secured court authorization to seize more than $1.2 billion tied to the record $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist.
  • North Korean Attribution: U.S. authorities continue to link major cryptocurrency thefts, including TraderTraitor and FaceStealer attacks, to North Korean state-backed hackers.
  • Combined Efforts: U.S. government agencies and private sector partners have successfully frozen a combined total of over $2.7 billion in stolen assets.

Why It Matters

The operation underscores the ongoing vulnerabilities within the global digital asset ecosystem and highlights how state actors leverage cybercrime to bypass international sanctions. U.S. officials emphasize that North Korea relies heavily on illicit cryptocurrency schemes to generate revenue for its regime, including its banned weapons programs. Law enforcement agencies maintain that aggressive asset freezes and court-authorized seizures serve as a critical defense mechanism against sophisticated international cyber syndicates attempting to launder stolen capital.
